THE ESSENTIALS

What is an Employment Contract?

An Employment Contract establishes the legal framework between your business and a new employee. It explicitly details the job role, working hours, salary, and benefits.

Beyond basic terms, it shields your company from unfair dismissal claims and secures your proprietary information.

Key Protections

  • **IP Ownership:** Automatic transfer of employee creations.
  • **Termination:** Clear terms protecting against unlawful dismissal claims.
  • **Confidentiality:** Restricts sharing of internal business data.
THE RISK

Hiring Without a Formal Agreement

Relying on verbal agreements with staff exposes your business to catastrophic employment tribunals.

Tribunal Claims

Without clear terms, employees can claim unfair dismissal or owed benefits, leading to costly legal battles.

IP Theft

Employees might claim ownership over the code or processes they developed while on your payroll.

Data Leaks

Lack of confidentiality clauses allows departing staff to take client lists to competitors.

THE SOLUTION

Contract Inclusions

Every clause is structured to protect your business from common employment disputes.

Role & Duties

Clearly defined job description, reporting lines, and expected responsibilities.

Remuneration

Structured salary, bonus structures, and statutory deductions.

Working Hours

Explicit definitions of normal working hours, overtime, and remote working policies.

Leave Entitlements

Detailed provisions for annual leave, sick pay, and maternity/paternity rights.

Notice Periods

Clear guidelines on resignation and termination procedures.

Post-Employment Restraints

Non-compete and non-solicitation clauses to protect your business post-departure.
